last.verdict: Bitcoin's rebound produced a $409.7 million profit, but the media business still loses money and nearly $1 billion of notes may need repaying.

takeaways.label: Profit is bitcoin, not business
takeaways.text: Net income was $409.7 million, driven by non-cash gains: $378.1 million on digital assets after bitcoin rose about 42% in the quarter. Revenue was only about $3 million.

takeaways.label: Note repayment unresolved
takeaways.text: Holders of nearly $1 billion in convertible notes can demand repayment starting Nov. 30. Management cannot say how much will be repaid, plans cash and credit, and says no new equity is planned.

takeaways.label: TAE merger on schedule
takeaways.text: Shareholders vote Dec. 14 on the fusion-energy merger, with closing targeted by year-end. The share count would roughly double from about 300 million to about 600 million.

takeaways.label: Costs fell, media still loses
takeaways.text: Operating expenses fell 45% from the prior quarter to $26.5 million, mostly on lower legal fees. Adjusted EBITDA was still a $12.3 million loss on about $3 million revenue.

history.verdict: Trump Media is now mostly a bitcoin holder and a fusion-merger bet, with a tiny $1.7 million-a-quarter media business.

takeaways.label: Bitcoin drives the loss
takeaways.text: The $238.1 million quarterly net loss came mostly from $190.4 million of non-cash bitcoin and stock losses. Revenue was only $1.7 million, up 89%.

takeaways.label: TAE merger is the plan
takeaways.text: Management calls the fusion-company merger the most important driver of value. It targets a Q4 2026 close but would not commit to a date, and the filing is still pending.

takeaways.label: Crypto.com deal dropped
takeaways.text: The planned Crypto.com/Yorkville combination was terminated, and the Crypto.com tie-up became a marketing deal. The company also paused its in-house bitcoin yield strategy for third-party management.

takeaways.label: Nearly $1B debt coming due
takeaways.text: Nearly $1 billion of convertible notes come due. Management says the balance sheet can cover them but gave no repayment plan. Liquid cash and short-term investments exceed $400 million.
